generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and sport science, looking out for learning by doing changes how you read your course. A coaching placement with a local club, a lab session testing an athlete's fitness, or fieldwork measuring performance are all chances to learn by doing. Each time one comes up, you can name it, work out its form, and ask what it could give you.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science students are offered a coaching placement and a lab project testing athletes. One takes both on without thinking about what they are. The other names each as learning by doing, sees that one is a placement and the other a lab project, and works out what each could teach. By the end, the second student has real coaching experience and lab skills to show an employer.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and sport science, learning by doing appears as coaching placements, lab work, fieldwork and volunteering at events. When you bring the three ideas together, you can spot each chance, name its form, and see what it offers your development. That habit helps you build towards the career in sport you are aiming for.

check.body: A student spots a live project in their course, names it as learning by doing, sees it could build real skills, and signs up. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: They brought the three ideas together as one practice: they recognised the chance, placed its form, and saw what it offered.
_items.feedback: Yes. Naming it, placing its form and seeing its benefit is the one practice at work.

_items.text: They skipped straight to signing up without knowing what the project was.
_items.feedback: They did name it as learning by doing first. That is part of the practice.

_items.text: They treated the project as ordinary classroom study.
_items.feedback: They saw it as learning by doing, which is the opposite of ordinary classroom study.

_items.text: They only looked at the benefits and ignored what the project actually was.
_items.feedback: They named it and placed its form too, not only its benefits.
